parameter.name: LAW_DEGREE
parameter.what: issue #257: the cutoff -> coefficient tuning law. 0 is the shipped CUT_TRIM * fcr (DR 0011); 3 and 4 are polynomials in f/SR refitted to the linearised loop (ladder_headroom.refit_tuning).

objective.name: worst |offset| on the select grid
objective.why: the law is a function of cutoff only, so it is judged by the worst single point's distance from the commanded cutoff with the resonance correction held fixed; the correction cannot reach a cutoff-dependent error.

range_basis: 0 is the law that ships today; 3 is fcr's own shape refitted (same build-time cost); 4 is the quartic docs/ladder-rung1-audit.md section 3 sized at 0.023 % law error. Higher degrees chase a law error already below the ring's own per-cutoff spread.
Committed in docs/res-tuning/plan.json (commit dcbc2e1) before any point was measured.

decision_rule.why: pre-registered in docs/res-tuning/plan.json: the estimator is qualified to 1 cent, so a few cents is the granularity at which two candidates are distinguishable at the 5-20 cent level this objective lives at.

evidence.instrument: model/res_tuning.py ring_frequency on reference_rigs.OurLadder's free ring (fixed-point model, 0.8 s, last 60 %); estimator qualified to 0.04 c on synthetic signals of known frequency.

prediction.basis: stated in docs/res-tuning/plan.json before the sweep: the shipped law's ~1 % S-shaped residual (~17 c) is a function of cutoff the correction cannot touch, so 0 separates; the quartic's 0.2 pp gain over the cubic is under the ring's ~1.1 pp per-cutoff spread, so 3 and 4 do not.

verdict.summary: As predicted: refitting the law removes a third of the worst error (18.8 -> 12.3 c); cubic and quartic are the same to the cent. The pre-registered selection rule (lowest degree in the best run) picks 3, which is fcr's own shape and build-time cost.

limits: Model-level only: the parameter lives in model/res_tuning.py's candidate, not yet in rtl-sketch/voice_dp.v or the numeric contract (spec/decision-records/0024). The gate checks the candidate's value, which is what a later RTL change must carry.

Measured on the SELECT grid (7 cutoffs 100..6400 Hz x 7 resonances 1.02..2.00). The selected candidate was then validated once on the untouched grid in docs/res-tuning/validation.txt; that grid had no part in this choice.
The 12.3 c floor shared by 3 and 4 is set by a single cutoff-dependent residual neither law removes; it is not a law-degree question.
